This filter weighed exactly the same after one year of use (10 oz.). So I can only conclude that it did not accumulate sediment and copper, zinc, etc. Therefore, it may be completely useless.

Ok now I know this will work for clothes etc because I am going to describe my first use of the thing, and you will think I am nutz.

Sick cat, basically permanent colitis and has these flare ups which require her to be crated (it's a big crate with room for a bed and a cat box etc so keep the OMG down guys I freaking love my cat) and she generally has at least one accident per day or more on the blankets, which are fleece. The upside is I don't find myself in midair in my bathroom with cat diarrhea on my foot just before slamming back first into the stuff. Oh and it's not EVERYWHERE ELSE.
So I have cut up fleece blankets, they get a wipe and a fold and after a few days that's it they have stuff all over them including stuck on litter etc so they go in the bag and a new one goes in.
After a while I have a bunch of dirty blankets. SO I tried this tool on THEM. Two were full sized "throw" blankets, the rest have been cut in half. Now we are talking disgusting nasty gunk here folks. IN a 5 gallon bucket, I cleaned these things, changing the water each time. Then rinse. These blankets came out CLEAN and I mean like I would sleep on the things. Impressed.
So if you want to clean some socks and shirts etc, go for it. This is solidly built. You will need a handle, I just used a push broom handle so I can stand up and do it in a container on the floor in the tub.

I've seen this on many different Off Grid type TV shows and when my Washing Machine broke I decided I was going to give this a try before I bought another washer. I have had this a Month now and I am not going to waste the $500+ Dollars on another Washing Machine. There are two boys, my Husband so 3 boys ;) along with 5 dogs, =ing 5 dog beds, 5 Cats and 5 Ferrets. All of the animal bedding gets washed once a week and I do the normal daily laundry. I found putting a normal batch of laundry into the bathtub and washing in there has got my clothes and bedding much cleaner than my 4 year old Whirlpool Washing Machine ever did. I bought a nice expandable painters pole (as this does not have a pole with it) and it has proven to be the best money I have spent in quite sometime.

Ok, I love this clothes washer, but I did modify it just a bit.  I only use the inside.  I find the top part kind of bulky and awkward so I took the whole thing apart and just use the colander like part.  I had it screwed into an old plastic mop handles, but they kept breaking off at the screw end.  I just use a wooden plunger handle now.  I live in an apartment and usually wait a couple of weeks before throwing everything into the bath tub. It's a big load!  I agitate (vigorously) the load and let it sit for awhile and repeat this process once or twice more.  I use a portable spin dryer to get all the soapy water out before adding everything back into the tub for the rinse.  I use the mobile washer again to get the clothes rinsed.  I spin dry the clothes and then hang them up to dry.  Yeah, it is more work and takes longer this way, but I prefer this to the laundry mat.  I can putz around the apartment while the clothes are soaking during the wash and rinse 'cycle.'  Before I started using the Breathing Mobile Washer I just agitated the clothes with my hands and arms or used an old mop handle.  I really like the way the breathing mobile washer gets the soapy water into the clothes.  It's just as good during the rinse cycle.

This will get your clothes so clean they'll feel weird & squeaky, even when they are dry! This gets them cleaner than any washing machine! I got this thinking it'd be a temporary thing I could use till I got my mini machine. After using it once, I decided not to bother getting a machine at all. I've been taking clothes out of drawers that I had put away clean in order to rewash them with this and see what happened- it never fails to shock me when I see all the dirt run out in the rinse water! It is able to clean "clean" clothes even cleaner than I thought they already were! Cheap and great! Go to a home improvement warehouse or Amazon and get a long pole for it (or use a broomstick) and wear cloves so you don't get calluses and plunge away!!

Well, maybe love is a bit much for something the is tied to cleaning and work.  I grew up in Alaska bush country so am quite familiar with washing by hand.  That was many years ago and this is now, so now I can get my exercise while doing a necessary task of laundry.  I got this unit for a long term trip in an RV.  I camp usually in remote camp sites or boondock.  In the  past I have done laundry in laundromats with some disastrous results like; finding out you have cleaned the tar out of a washer with your clothes or.... collecting cat? dog? sasquatch? hair.  When I need to do laundry its a simple process.  Bucket, soap, water, clothes, exercise, rinse, repeat.  I do cheat with Nina (s s d) If you want your clothes really clean do it when you are angry.  Really can get your heart rate up.  I have not found the solution for the head to tend to want to spin off but I have not found it to be a real problem.  It only seems to do it when I have a large bulky wash.  I am sure its an easy fix but I really have not taken the time to do it.  I am also working on various handles combinations.  When I get back to base camp I will see if another handle will do ok for the unscrewing and also if it will be as good as my current one regarding comfort.  At 6ft2 a long handle is a must.  If you are lonely just leave the washer out on a picnic table and see what happens.  Could lead to conversations or scare visitors away .

When my washing machine died while I was getting ready to move, I decided to try this instead of getting another machine.
To begin with, I bought a washtub to go in my bathtub so I could do small loads. The tub was too large for my cast-iron tub, and rocked. If you should go the same route, be sure to measure your bathtub and get a washtub that will fit flat on the floor.
Secondly, I did not find that it was very effective at getting the clothes clean. A lot of work, filling the washtub, using the plunger (pardon me, "mobile washer"), emptying the water, refilling it and rinsing the clothes several times, squeezing them out and putting them in the dryer, for no better results than I got. It may be that I just didn't have the stamina to keep at it long enough.

Took this camping.  So glad I did. My niece spit up a lot,  and had several blowouts.  I used this in my 5 gallon bucket with a hole in the lid. Got out all the stains.  Not sure if that was from this device or my SA-8 laundry soap

I have had this, or one almost like it (gotten from Amazon), and used it for about 3 years now after our automatic washing machine stopped working.  We're both retired now so don't need business attire and we don't seem to mess up our clothes as much as we used to so there's less to wash.  It works.  I bought a couple cheap 5 gal. paint buckets at the hardware store and use them--fill them up and let the items soak overnight (or at least for 4+ hours), then use this blue thing to bash the items a bit.  I would say I bash for less then a minute (I imagine I'm churning butter just so I don't give up), then pour out the dirty water, refill with clean water, bash it a bit more, pour out that water and dump the wet items into a very big (cheap) colander/strainer I set in the bathroom sink (all washing and rinsing are done in the bathtub so I can splash all I want).  I do sheets too or one sheet at a time, and towels (1 bath, 2 smaller hand towels).  I can't do a whole lot of clothes at once, pair of jeans, couple of t-shirts, couple of underwear--I do maybe 2 washing per week of only our clothing.  It cleans well but I pre-treat any real stains and sometimes use baking soda when needed.  Then after it's drained an hour to get the drippy water out, everything goes into a small spin dryer (which makes a huge difference, we initially had problems with the clothes not drying thoroughly enough in the dryer unless you ran the dryer for 3 hours or more; the spin dryer squeezes out a lot

I have tried several filter by different companies and this one is by far the better of them. This one is simple to install just remove the old one by turning it counter clockwise and then put this one in its place and twist about 1/4 turn clockwise. You will feel it tighten up.When finished installing the filter I put my water pitcher under the water spout and let it run til the air is out of the system which is about 2 or 3 minutes. I didn't see any thing floating in my water like a few others stated in their review, mine was clear from the start, and had no odor or taste. I highly recommend this filter. And knowing its made in the USA helps a lot.
